topIssues.title: opgeth-decoupling: migrate 19 direct L2 ethclient call sites in op-e2e
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Part of #20265 → #20257. See plan §13 in the op-geth decoupling doc (PR #19767).

## Scope

19 call sites across 9 files that call `ethclient.BlockByNumber` / `BlockByHash` / `TransactionByHash` against an **L2** endpoint — these fail under upstream go-ethereum due to deposit-tx decoding:

- `op-e2e/actions/proofs/isthmus_fork_test.go` (3 sites)
- `op-e2e/actions/upgrades/ecotone_fork_test.go` (3 sites)
- `op-e2e/actions/helpers/user.go` (2 sites — `CrossLayerUser`)
- `op-e2e/faultproofs/cannon_benchmark_test.go` (1 site)
- `op-e2e/interop/interop_test.go` (1 site, `BlockByHash`)
- `op-e2e/system/bridge/validity_test.go` (1 site)
- `op-e2e/system/conductor/system_adminrpc_test.go` (3 sites)
- `op-e2e/system/fees/` (3 sites in `fees_test.go`, `l1info_test.go`)
- `op-e2e/system/verifier/legacy_pending_test.go` (2 sites)

Also: change `op-e2e/system/e2esys.SystemConfig.L2Client` from `*ethclient.Client` to `apis.EthClient`.

For each site: migrate to `apis.EthClient` or the header-only variant from #20272 if only height matters.

topIssues.title: opgeth-decoupling: split op-e2e/e2eutils/geth/wait.go into header-only and full-block variants
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Part of #20265 → #20257. See plan §13 in the op-geth decoupling doc (PR #19767).

## Scope

- Add `WaitForBlockHeight(num, client)` returning `*types.Header` via `HeaderByNumber` — L2-safe under upstream (headers don't carry txs).
- Migrate callers that only use the returned block for side-effect/height checks (`_, err := WaitForBlock(...)`) to the new header variant — majority of ~26 callers.
- Keep `WaitForBlock` returning `*types.Block` for the small set that reads block body fields (e.g. `op-e2e/system/fees/eip1559params_test.go`); migrate its underlying client to `apis.EthClient` so deposit txs decode.
- `WaitForTransaction` return type → `*optypes.Receipt` (ripples from #20264).
- `WaitUntilTransactionNotFound`: callers use non-deposit user txs; document the L2-deposit failure mode and migrate if a call site ever targets a deposit tx hash.

Blocked on: #20264.

topIssues.title: kona-node: prevent delegated finalized-head regression
topIssues.author: joshklop
topIssues.body:
A stale delegated source can make Kona request a backward finalized-head update. This is the finalized-monotonicity scope of the delegated derivation parity tracker.

## Reproduction

With local unsafe=30, safe=20, finalized=10, a delegate reports an existing finalized block 5. FinalizeTask checks only that the target is no higher than safe, sends an FCU with finalized=5, and records finalized=5 if EL returns VALID.

The actual Kona engine unit test proves the backward request and acceptance logic. It does **not** establish that real op-reth accepts a finalized regression. EL rejection could instead cause recovery errors.

Compare [Kona finalization](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/49efa52bcb3ecaeea390d333de63b37b8650aa75/rust/kona/crates/node/engine/src/task_queue/tasks/finalize/task.rs#L32-L75) with [op-node's external finalized monotonicity guard](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/4f0f0eaf92b923f61d11a9405b88880999399529/op-node/rollup/engine/engine_controller.go#L1535-L1538).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Older finalized references do not emit backward FCUs or regress CL finalized state.
- [ ] Repeated identical finalized references remain harmless while allowing legitimate pending EL synchronization.
- [ ] Conflicting hashes at the current finalized height are rejected safely rather than silently replacing finality.
- [ ] Preserve hash-pinned lookup, height validation, and safe/finalized ordering checks.
- [ ] Cover older, identical, conflicting-same-height, and legitimate advancing targets.
- [ ] Keep the implementation independent of catch-up liveness and forkchoice delivery/retry fixes.

Confirmed on deployed `49efa52` and PR #23627 tip `2763f5e`; relevant code is unchanged on develop `cfec650e57`. Implement as an independent PR against develop.

Parent tracker: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/545 (target November 5, 2026).

topIssues.title: kona-node: reliably deliver and retry delegated forkchoice updates
topIssues.author: joshklop
topIssues.body:
Delegated safe-head updates are not reliably delivered to the execution client, and SYNCING responses suppress retries. These are related forkchoice-delivery problems in the delegated derivation parity tracker.

## Reproductions

1. Local unsafe=20, safe=0, finalized=0; delegate safe=10, finalized=0; matching block 10 already exists locally. BlockInfo consolidation takes the intermediate-span branch, changes CL safe/local-safe to 10, and emits no FCU. Unchanged finalization then short-circuits synchronization. With no unsafe production/import, EL safe remains behind CL safe.
2. Synchronization requests changed heads and receives SYNCING. Kona records the requested state. An identical subsequent request returns without calling the Engine API, even if the EL can now apply it. This matches the central pattern fixed in op-node https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20310.

Both behaviors were reproduced with actual kona-engine tasks and strict mocked Engine API responses. New block production often masks the problem; a live recovery stall has not been demonstrated.

Sources: [BlockInfo consolidation](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/49efa52bcb3ecaeea390d333de63b37b8650aa75/rust/kona/crates/node/engine/src/task_queue/tasks/consolidate/task.rs#L196-L218), [synchronization](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/49efa52bcb3ecaeea390d333de63b37b8650aa75/rust/kona/crates/node/engine/src/task_queue/tasks/synchronize/helper.rs#L25-L88).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Delegated safe promotion reaches EL even when unsafe/finalized do not change.
- [ ] Preserve intentional batching of intermediate native Attributes updates.
- [ ] Distinguish requested forkchoice from successfully applied forkchoice, or provide an equally sound retry mechanism.
- [ ] SYNCING leaves pending work and identical requests can reach EL again; cover SYNCING then VALID with unchanged targets.
- [ ] Recovery progresses without relying on new unsafe blocks, without busy-looping or treating transient SYNCING as fatal.
- [ ] Test changed-target behavior and ensure successful VALID updates do not cause unnecessary repeated FCUs.
- [ ] Keep invalid forkchoice/protocol errors distinct from temporary EL sync.

Confirmed on deployed `49efa52` and PR #23627 tip `2763f5e`; relevant code is unchanged on develop `cfec650e57`. Implement as an independent PR against develop.

Parent tracker: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/545 (target November 5, 2026).

topPRs.title: contracts-bedrock: add ComplianceModule bridge hook
topPRs.author: lumoswiz
topPRs.body:
**Description**

Adds `ComplianceModule` so deposits and withdrawals can wait for policy clearance, then complete on their original terms. The module holds deferred value, and a replaceable policy decides whether it can move.

**Tests**

Adds unit, fuzz and invariant coverage, real Portal comparisons of held and direct transfers, and shared withdrawal item ID vectors for the bridge screener.

**Additional context**

The module uses its own `ProxyAdmin` outside OPCM to separate custody upgrade authority from policy management. The policy implementation and broader integration coverage follow separately.

**Metadata**

- Closes ethereum-optimism/optimism-private#742

topPRs.title: op-zk-proposer: local CUDA proof provider and op-zk-proposer-cuda image
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
Adds `OP_ZK_PROPOSER_PROOF_PROVIDER=local-cuda`, a self-hosted backup for an SPN outage (ethereum-optimism/proofs-team#51). Proofs come from SP1's `sp1-gpu-server`, one per CUDA device, through the existing request/wait flow. A new amd64 image, `op-zk-proposer-cuda`, adds the server, the CUDA 12.8 runtime, and the v6.1.0 PLONK circuits to the existing binary.

The proposer starts each server itself and speaks the public `sp1_cuda::api` socket protocol, instead of using the SP1 SDK's CUDA client, which downloads a missing or mismatched server from GitHub at runtime. A startup `--version` check keeps the server and the protocol types on the linked SP1 version, and the server gets no `OP_ZK_PROPOSER_*` variables.

A CPU pre-execution enforces the cycle and memory limits before a request reaches a GPU and classifies failures as SPN does, so bisection and chain splitting work unchanged. Other local failures are resubmitted. A broken GPU server connection exits the process, so every server stops and the pod restarts; local proof progress is in memory and is lost. Network and mock mode do not change. The README's "Local CUDA proving" section covers sizing, `/dev/shm`, and known limits (queued stdin memory, no hung-server detection, no release tag for the CUDA image).

Testing: unit tests drive the provider through a scripted GPU server and executor, and the socket client against a fake server. No real GPU proof has run, and this PR's CI is the first melange/apko build of the new image.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

topPRs.title: contracts-bedrock: add ComplianceModule end-to-end tests
topPRs.author: 0xarktos
topPRs.body:
**Description**

Adds end-to-end Foundry tests that run the Portal, the L1StandardBridge, the L1CrossDomainMessenger, the ComplianceModule and VisionPolicyV1 together. The module is deployed and set as the Portal's bridge hook through a real OPCM upgrade, and VisionPolicyV1 makes every screening decision.

A shared `ComplianceIntegration_TestInit` deploys the system and provides helpers to deposit through the real entry points, read held deposits and withdrawals back from the module's `Held` event, build and prove withdrawals, and assert custody on the Portal, the bridge and the module.

**Tests**

30 integration tests in `test/integration`, gated on `DEV_FEATURE__BRIDGE_HOOK`:

- Deposits and withdrawals of ETH, escrowed ERC20, mintable ERC20 and zero-value messages run through hold, clearance and completion. Each held item is compared with the same item proceeding directly: a deposit must publish an identical `TransactionDeposited`, and a withdrawal must make an identical call with the same `l2Sender` (FM5).
- A deposit from a contract is held and completed with its aliased sender, while the policy screens the contract's own address.
- Every completed deposit is checked against the terms of its held item, so a completion cannot publish a different sender, target, value, gas limit or data.
- `clearAndCompleteDeposit` and `clearAndCompleteWithdrawal` run through `multicall`. One entry that cannot complete reverts the whole batch, and the other entry completes when the batch is sent again without it (Policy FM5).
- Failures and retries: a reverting withdrawal target, a failed messenger relay replayed later, a completion over the block's deposit gas limit, duplicate completions, and revoked or expired verdicts. Each checks balances, escrow and held records.
- Policy outcomes seen through the Portal: rejection before the hold delay, immediate holds for denied parties and expired verdicts, the Fee Vault rule, and the pause.
- Hook lifecycle: deployment wiring and ownership, disable with a nonce cutoff and re-enable, and hook removal followed by setting the same module again and completing the items held before (FM18).
- Upgrades: an OPCM upgrade, a module upgrade and a policy swap each keep held funds, verdicts and records, and the held items complete afterward on their held terms.

**Additional context**

- Devnet tests, op-deployer flows and resuming interrupted deployments are not part of this PR.
- The tests deploy the module and policy inline.
- Deposits are asserted up to the `TransactionDeposited` event on L1. L2 execution is left to the devnet tests.
- The test deployment respects a game type that its OPCM config does not enable, so the upgrade helper overrides the respected game type for the upgrade and restores it afterward.
- The tests run in the `BRIDGE_HOOK` entry of the CI dev-feature matrix and skip elsewhere, because OPCM rejects a bridge hook while the feature is off.

**Metadata**

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism-private/issues/746

topPRs.title: kona-engine!: deliver and retry delegated forkchoice updates
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
A kona-node following a delegate could leave the execution layer's safe head behind its own, and a SYNCING answer stopped it from retrying an unchanged forkchoice. This PR delivers every delegated safe head and retries until the execution layer answers VALID.

Follows up on #23680.
Closes #23676
Part of ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#545

**Changes**
- Delegated safe heads always send a forkchoice update; only derived blocks inside a span batch defer it. Before, `ConsolidateInput::BlockInfo` took the intermediate-span path, moved the labels without an FCU, and an unchanged finalized head then skipped the update.
- The engine records whether the execution layer answered VALID or SYNCING (`EngineState::forkchoice_status`), and skips an identical update only after VALID. Before, a SYNCING answer suppressed every retry, the same problem op-node fixed in #20310.
- A reset always resends its forkchoice.
- The delegate's 4s poll repeats the target, so it is the retry; the engine actor is unchanged. SYNCING from gossip inserts still moves the unsafe head; that is tracked in ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#574.
- `start_build` does not record its VALID answer. A build's FCU has head = parent, which already matches the applied forkchoice, so recording it would only add a `&mut EngineState` parameter.

**Tests**
- `synchronize_skips_only_an_applied_forkchoice`: rstest table over Unsent, Applied (same and different target), Syncing, SYNCING answers, INVALID and `-38002`, asserting whether an FCU is sent, the resulting status and the error severity.
- `unchanged_target_is_resent_after_syncing_until_valid`: three identical requests make exactly two FCUs (SYNCING, then VALID).
- `delegated_safe_head_reaches_execution_layer_with_finalized_unchanged`: reproduction 1 from the issue.
- `span_batch_sends_forkchoice_only_at_its_last_block`: native span batching is preserved.
- `reset_resends_previously_applied_forkchoice`.
- `delegated_safe_head_is_resent_after_syncing_until_applied`: a real `EngineActor` receives the same delegated safe head three times; the EL answers SYNCING, then VALID, and no third FCU is sent.

Each production change was reverted in turn and the corresponding tests fail. 386 kona-engine and kona-node-service tests pass under nextest; clippy (`-D warnings`, including kona-rpc) is clean.

**Interaction with the sibling fixes.** #23899 (finalized monotonicity) has identical-target cases that expect no FCU; whichever of the two lands second seeds those states as applied.

BREAKING CHANGE: `EngineState` has a new public field, `forkchoice_status`. Code that builds `EngineState` with a struct literal must set it (normally `ForkchoiceStatus::Unsent`) or use `..Default::default()`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
